- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak or adjust downward by 2–4 days.
- In high sentiment + low historical volatility, model often underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and model shows strong upward trend, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 2–4 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings) and model follows sentiment closely, model often misjudges mean reversion; apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price increases; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment is high but model forecast is flat or declining, model is ignoring sentiment; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to underestimate price when sentiment is high and historical price is trending down; add 1–2% upward bias for next 3–5 days if sentiment >0.6 and price is falling.
